task.goal: Compile the SPV-SYM-Symbolic SuperVisual harness -- a single-frame portrait card that carries its argument through one symbolic device (before/after gesture split, double-exposure wealth overlay, numbered listicle, or persona-identification grid) -- into a governed Builder contract, preserving the format's real visual-syntax lineage.
task.success_condition: The exported PortableAtomicHarnessDefinition binds to category_id 'supervisuals', preserves all activative_input lineage refs unmutated, and carries this harness's wrong_reading_locks into category_binding.wrong_reading_locks so they survive into campaign execution.
task.atomic_boundary: One ratified SPV-SYM-Symbolic reference set (eleven portrait/listicle/grid specimens plus the Drill-me doctrine pair) becomes one structural Builder contract. No media is generated, no campaign is executed, and no per-client semantic content is attached at this step.

source_expression_moment.description: The single quote line, listicle headline, or persona-identification prompt this SuperVisual will render for one runtime pass -- e.g. a struggle-to-triumph line, a numbered 'mistakes' or 'don't say / say' list, or a 'which one are you' grid caption.

voice_context.description: Runtime brand-voice parameters for this render: palette family (gold/black authority, red/orange warning, blue wealth duotone), gesture register (struggle, triumph, warning stare, aspirational drive), and single-quote vs numbered-listicle vs persona-grid layout choice.

rendered_supervisual_spec.description: The composed single-frame spec (component bboxes, role/why bindings, watermark placement, forbidden-pattern checks) ready to hand to the render runtime. Structural only -- no rasterized media.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer scrolls past personal-brand authority content constantly; this format has one static frame to make the viewer feel personally addressed -- through a gesture, a listicle item, or a persona grid -- before they swipe past.
activative_input.stance: Direct, declarative, and symbolically compressed -- one gesture, one overlay, or one list stands in for the whole argument.
stakes: the viewer's sense of being personally seen
accurate representation of the mentor's stated experience
identity_urges: want the shortcut without losing self-respect
want to be told the truth plainly
activative_input.participation_design: A single static frame carries either a symbolic before/after gesture, a numbered list, or a persona-identification grid, inviting the viewer to privately locate themselves in it -- and, for the grid sub-pattern, to tag a friend in the comments.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer recognizes themselves in the gesture, list item, or persona and feels the mentor is speaking directly to their specific situation.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Pause the scroll and read the full list or caption before swiping past.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let the before/after split-portrait (visible struggle gesture next to visible triumph gesture) be read as a literal, dated timeline of the mentor's own biography -- it is a symbolic emotional-state device, not a factual claim about a specific past event.

Do not let numbered 'mistakes' or 'reasons' listicles be read as exhaustive, clinically-validated business, financial, or psychological advice -- they are motivational framing, not licensed counsel, and must not imply guaranteed outcomes.

Do not let money/wealth double-exposure overlays (currency, luxury vehicles) be read as a specific income claim, earnings promise, or guarantee of financial results -- they are aspirational symbolism only.

Do not let the judgmental 'stay away from people who...' listicle be read as targeted advice to sever specific named relationships, or as license to harass any real, identifiable person -- it is a self-accountability prompt aimed at the viewer's own habits.
Do not let the persona-identification grid ('which one are you') be read as a validated personality or psychological assessment -- it is a playful, non-clinical self-identification engagement device.
